sentiment.summary: Ethereum-related coverage in the 30-day window was largely constructive: Fidelity filed to add staking and quarterly cash distributions to its ether ETF, Goldman Sachs’s planned NEOS acquisition includes Ether-linked income funds, and the Ethereum Foundation announced a Trillion Dollar Security grant for WEBCAT plus a board appointment. The main offset is Russia moving to confine retail crypto trading to bitcoin, ether and USDT with purchase caps for non-qualified investors.

tags.label: ETF staking and institutional products
tags.why: Fidelity filed to add staking to its ether ETF, keeping 85% of rewards in the fund with quarterly cash distributions planned, and Goldman Sachs’s NEOS deal would add Ether-linked income funds.

tags.label: Retail trading limits
tags.why: Russia moved to restrict retail crypto trading to bitcoin, ether and USDT, with a 300,000-ruble annual purchase limit per intermediary for non-qualified investors.

tags.label: Security tooling grant
tags.why: The Ethereum Foundation’s Trillion Dollar Security initiative allocated a grant to Freedom of the Press Foundation to continue developing WEBCAT, an open-source tool for verifying website-served code.

tags.label: Foundation board
tags.why: The Ethereum Foundation said pcaversaccio joined its Board, citing long-time ecosystem contribution, SEAL 911 leadership, and Silviculture Society membership.

sentiment.coverage_note: Cointelegraph, CoinDesk, and Ethereum Foundation RSS were ok and supplied the usable records; Reddit auth-failed and YouTube and grounding returned no-results. One Cointelegraph item (CFTC/Kalshi) did not mention Ethereum and was not used. Fidelity staking was reported by both Cointelegraph and CoinDesk.
